arts: The 15 'Visual Arts' units are Grade 3-4 geography and history (globe, continents, states of India, early humans, agriculture, trade), not art: a global 'art'->'Visual arts' replacement in the source also corrupted words ('PVisual artsicipation', 'EVisual artsh', 'bVisual artser'); they are mapped by their text to World Around Us rows, and the school's actual visual-arts programme is absent from the unit map except the Memory Drawing and Doodle & Describe routines.

NCF preparatory PE rows carry both nested standards, LS-1 (CG-3..6) and LS-2 (CG-1..2), which repeat each other almost verbatim and are mapped identically; LS-2's own CG-3 (mental engagement, C-3.1/3.2) collided with LS-1's CG-3 id and is missing from ncf_competencies.json.

NCERT has no art or HPE outcomes below Class 9, so every preparatory and middle competency has an empty ncert list; 25 Class 9-10 art outcomes (care of materials and instruments, self-confidence, teamwork values, artists' lives, planning-to-performance) state what NCF-SE places in the middle stage and are mapped to those middle C rows, which therefore carry Class 9-10 evidence.

Vocational education has no preparatory rows and no NCERT outcomes; Primary Computing G3-4 units on algorithms, loops, debugging and data-driven problem solving map to ncf.math.P.CG-4 (the only NCF row naming computational thinking, no C fits), while networks, hardware, AI and data-handling units get no competency because NCF preparatory mathematics has no data-handling row.

Champak (Hindi reading) is mapped to R2 preparatory rows on the assumption that English is R1 at the school; if Hindi is R3 there is no preparatory R3 row to use. G1-2 bands of computing and routines use foundational domain rows (excluded from the graded lists as instructed), so mixed-band units carry one foundational and one preparatory target.

The 49 LS-2 rows take their LS-1 twin's capabilities, grades and Class 9-10 evidence where the text matches; where the minimum standard asks less the grades widen to the whole stage (pe.ls2.M.C-3.1 simple strategies; pe.ls2.S.C-2.1 without 'in the long term'; pe.ls2.S.C-3.1 without the mid-game plan C). NCERT evidence is given for secondary rows only, and pe.ls2.S.C-1.3 (own activity plan), S.C-2.6, S.C-3.1 and S.C-4.1 have no Class 9-10 outcome.

Both art mix-ups come from the extraction, not the units: in the school's sheets Visual Arts, Geography and History are term sub-blocks of the Global Perspectives strand, and the extraction labels every block 'Global perspectives' except the G3-G4 term-1 Geography/History blocks, which it labels 'Visual Arts'. The sub-block header rows became units: unit.115 merges four art units across G1-G3 (Introduction to Visual Arts, My Dream House, Lines Around Us, Paper Sculpture) and unit.420 two in G4; all are art, so each is mapped to the union. unit.438 is not art. It is the G4 copy of unit.303 'Natural Resources', split off by the 'Earth'->'EVisual artsh' garbling, and takes unit.303's rows (ncf.world.P.C-4.3, C-4.4); unit_subject_corrections.json wrongly marks it 'art'.

Gaps for the founders: the G1-G4 unit map has no music, dance or theatre unit (only rhymes inside English literacy), so no unit reaches ncf.fnd.F.C-12.2 or any preparatory music, theatre or dance row, and LS-2's variety across art forms (ncf.art.ls2.P.C-1.1) is met only in its visual part. Every art form or artist the G2-G4 units name is non-Indian (Aboriginal dot art, Japanese kites, African masks, papel picado, Scandinavian weaving, Starry Night); Warli in G1 is the one local form, so ncf.art.visual.P.C-4.2 (curiosity towards local art forms) has no unit.
foundational: Source parsing: CG-13 and C-13.1–13.4 carry area 'Aesthetic and Cultural Development' but are the NCF's 'Positive Learning Habits' (not a domain; the heading is glued to the end of C-12.5's text); a footnote is glued into C-11.2 and its text is cut at '(from C'; CG-9 carries a footnote mark ('languages1'). Fix at source before these texts reach a screen.

Languages: the NCF's Language 1 (CG-10) is taken as English, the medium, and Language 2 (CG-11) as Marathi/Hindi, so ncert.eng.* attaches to CG-9/CG-10 rows and none to CG-11 (the NCERT file has no Marathi or Hindi). For many children the home language is the reverse; the school should confirm, and also fix when the second script starts (C-11.1 given K2–G2, C-11.2 G1–G2).

Grades: developmental competencies (domains 1–7, 12, 13 and oral language) span N–G2 as the NCF's own outcome ladders do; where a text names an attainment (counting to 99, two-digit sums, reading passages, a paragraph, a second script) the grades are where the competency as worded is shown (K2 or G1 onwards) and its N/K1 precursors are not listed.

NCERT Classes 1–2 has no outcome for multiplication/division (C-8.7), reading fluency, poems or informational text (C-10.4, 10.6, 10.7), print concepts (C-10.2), composing songs (C-9.2) or narrating stories (C-9.6); its Class 2 writing ceiling is a sentence (eng.2.12) where the NCF asks a paragraph (C-10.8): the NCF is the higher bar. ncert.math.1.01 fuses two outcomes (classifying; counting to 20) and ncert.math.2.01 fuses six; the math seat should split them.

C-7.3 is the only foundational row feeding technology-and-ai; the NCF-FS means everyday and learning tools (scissors, magnifier, balance) before digital ones, so it should not be read as a screen competency.
language: Which language is R1, R2 and R3 is the founders' decision: here English→R1 (foundational CG-10 'Language 1' rows for G1–G2), Hindi→R2 (foundational CG-11 'Language 2' rows for G1–G2), Marathi→R2 for its content units and R3 for its Grade-4 script units; every id can be re-pointed wholesale.

NCF has no preparatory-stage R3 rows (a third language starts at Grade 6) and no R2 row for beginning a script after Grade 2, so the 14 Grade-4 Marathi script units (मुळाक्षरे, स्वरचिन्ह, सोळाखडी, जोडाक्षरे, अंकलेखन) sit on r3.S.C-5.1 (script and phonetics) and r3.M.C-2.1 (reading words) by text, two stages above the children; if Marathi becomes R2, re-point them to r2.P.C-2.1 and C-2.2.

The NCERT file holds English outcomes only, so every R2 and R3 row has an empty ncert list (NCERT's Hindi outcomes and Maharashtra's Marathi ones would fill them), and five R1 rows have no NCERT outcome at all: r1.P.C-5.1 library borrowing, r1.M.C-1.5 audio-visual content, r1.M.C-5.1 the phonetics and script of English, r1.S.C-4.3 language and identity, r1.S.C-4.5 tribal and regional languages.

NCERT keeps assessing reading aloud with pause and intonation up to class 10 (eng 3.03, 4.12, 7.02, 9.06) while NCF places fluency only at the foundational stage (fnd C-10.4), and R1 has no grammar, vocabulary, conversation or oral-presentation row after the preparatory stage, so some class 6–10 outcomes point at foundational or preparatory rows (fnd C-10.4; r1.P.C-1.1, C-1.3, C-4.1) and class 9–10 grammar at r1.M.C-3.1.

The school's G2 English (Roald Dahl novels, letters and emails, playscripts, book reviews) and G1–G2 Hindi (paragraph, dialogue and letter writing) run a stage ahead of the foundational rows they are mapped to; Play-Based Learning (units 062, 229, 377) and NCERT's language-lab visits, Sign Language and Braille outcomes are left empty with a why.
math: NCF-SE 2023 preparatory mathematics has no data-handling or probability goal, though NCERT Classes 3-5 (3.11, 4.12, 5.07) and the school's units 189, 017, 185, 316 teach them; they point to the nearest local row first, then to the later-stage row that is the content (M.C-5.2 data, S.C-6.2 probability). NCERT 8.19 (surface area/volume) likewise has no middle-stage NCF row and points to S.C-5.2.

The school runs ahead of NCF foundational: numbers to 200 in G1 (unit.008) and to 1,000 in G2 (unit.182) against NCF's 99 (F.C-8.5) and NCERT Class 2; fractions in G1-G2 (unit.011) have no foundational row (nearest: equal sharing F.C-8.7); negative numbers at G3-4 (unit.313) are the middle-stage M.C-1.3.

NCERT extraction artefacts: 7.03 and 8.08 are continuation fragments of 7.02 and 8.07 (fraction/expression symbols lost), 8.03 and 9.07 are truncated, 7.09 lost its ratios; each is mapped by the outcome it continues. NCF P.C-5.1 and M.C-10.1 texts carry stray section numbers '3.4.1.2' / '3.4.1.3'.

NCF secondary C-4.2 and C-7.3 are near-duplicates (both 'proves theorems using Euclid's axioms'); NCERT 9.05 evidences both. NCERT math has no outcome for location/maps (P.C-2.2), history of mathematics (P.C-5.1, M.CG-9, S.CG-10), tiling/fractals (M.C-4.3, M.C-4.4), Baudhayana-Pythagoras (M.C-4.2), numerical equality (M.C-2.1), computational thinking (M.CG-8, S.C-9.4) or optimisation (S.C-8.3), so those rows carry empty ncert lists.

unit.370's title is corrupted ('PVisual arts 2', 'quVisual artser-turns': a find/replace of 'art' hit 'Part' and 'quarter') and duplicates unit.188 for G4. unit.019/023/024 (fortnightly quiz, Ganit Diwas, Pi Day) are routines/celebrations left empty with a why; the bank visit (022), mental-math (020) and Olympiad (021) sessions carry numeracy objectives and are mapped.
science: The school's G3-G4 Science units (particles, energy transfers, Earth's structure, skeletons) are discipline-based, while NCF-SE 2023 gives the preparatory stage only World Around Us; their sole honest NCF homes are the familiarity rows ncf.world.P.C-7.1/C-7.2, so these units teach more content than NCF asks for at this stage and NCERT EVS 3-5 has no matching outcomes.

NCF has no vocational rows below the middle stage, so Home Science (stitching, weaving, cooking) is mapped to World Around Us (C-1.5 making objects, C-2.1/C-2.2 food and household systems, C-3.1 food safety, C-4.4 conserving resources) and foundational rows (C-1.1 nutritious food, C-1.4 safe tools, C-3.3 hand precision); a vocational target exists only from Grade 6.

Source defects: ncert.sci.6.04 and 6.05 are the same sentence (their targets were split across the three example investigations); unit.371 is a truncated duplicate of unit.322 ('and its Habitats'); unit.088-091 and unit.097-103 and unit.255-267 carry their objectives in the title field with empty samples.

NCERT's 2017/2019 outcomes give no evidence for several NCF rows, left with empty ncert lists: substance abuse (ncf.sci.M.C-4.4), open scientific questions (ncf.sci.M.C-9.2, ncf.sci.S.C-7.2), simple machines (ncf.sci.S.C-2.6), literature/arts and science (ncf.sci.S.C-5.1), science in music and dance (ncf.sci.S.C-5.3), and climate change or biodiversity collapse as such (ncf.env.S.C-1.1).

Environmental Education is graded G10 only (NCF-SE makes it a separate subject in Grade 10; its class 9 evidence is the interdependence outcome ncert.sci.9.17); five event units (Science Week, National Science Day, two field visits, Review and Assessment) are left without competencies with a 'why', since they have no written learning objectives.
social: 66 of the 97 'Global perspectives' units are not social science: 63 are Visual Arts units (unit.115-126, 137-147, 268-282, 291-302, 420-437; 420-437 also carry a find-and-replace garbling 'Visual arts' over 'Art'), unit.156 and unit.286 each merge two units into one record, unit.438 is 'Natural Resources' (G4) with 'Earth' garbled; all left unmapped with the reason in 'why'.

The school teaches geography and history in G1-G2 (states of India, continents, early humans, farming, trade) a stage ahead of NCF, whose foundational rows carry neither subject; those units are pinned to cognitive and socio-emotional rows (F.C-7.1, C-2.2, C-8.8, C-4.1, C-9.5) and the fit is weak. A better crosswalk needs either the preparatory World Around Us rows applied to G1-G2 or a school-defined target.

NCF's preparatory stage has no history or civics strand: World Around Us has no row for heroes, leaders, national symbols or inventions. The school's units on these are pinned to the nearest rows, C-2.3 (change over time as told by elders and local stories), C-2.1 (human-made systems) and C-4.7 (values and dispositions).

NCERT's 2019 secondary outcomes are five process bundles per class built on the CBSE syllabus. They give no evidence for NCF S.C-1.4 (indigenous knowledge systems, left empty) and only thin evidence for S.C-1.2, S.C-8.3 and S.C-9.1 (ancient India's chronology, economy and contributions). Grade 9 'Individuals in Society' has no NCERT outcomes of its own; its rows are evidenced by the class-9 process outcomes 9.02-9.05 only.

NCERT class-6 outcomes 6.01-6.03 (stars, planets, satellites; zones of the earth; day, night and seasons) sit on the science boundary and are mapped to M.C-6.1 (natural phenomena) as the nearest social-science row; the science seat may also claim them. 6.08 (superstitions about eclipses) is read as M.C-2.2, the continued prevalence of beliefs, examined against M.C-6.1.

nodes.text: Strong conceptual and procedural command of core subjects; can perform under examination conditions.

nodes.label: Counts a set of objects up to ten, touching each once and saying one number for each.
nodes.text: The educator watches the child's finger and voice keep step through the set.
nodes.counter: Recites numbers to ten faster than the finger moves, skipping or double-touching objects.

nodes.label: Reads a familiar word aloud from a word card or a label that has no picture beside it.
nodes.text: The educator points to a word on the word wall or a label and hears it read from its letters.
nodes.counter: Names the label by where it hangs and cannot read the same word on a card held elsewhere.

nodes.label: Exchanges ten single blocks for one ten-rod when asked how many tens are in a pile.
nodes.text: The educator sees the child make the exchange and name the rod as one ten.
nodes.counter: Moves blocks into a row of ten without naming it as one ten.

nodes.label: Retells a story just heard with its beginning, middle and end in the right order.
nodes.text: The educator hears the events come in the order the story had them.
nodes.counter: Names characters from the story without the events in order.

nodes.label: Sorts a mixed set of objects by a rule the educator names, and says the rule back.
nodes.text: The educator sees the sort match the rule and hears the child state it.
nodes.counter: Sorts by a rule of their own and cannot say what it was.

nodes.label: Writes or forms their own name and the numerals one to nine, on paper or with tiles, from memory, so another adult reads them back.
nodes.text: The educator sees no model in view and a second adult reads the name and numerals back, in any script the child is learning.
nodes.counter: Traces the name over a dotted model.

nodes.label: Uses a word taught this week in a sentence of their own about something in the room.
nodes.text: The educator hears the week's word in a sentence the child made, about a thing in view.
nodes.counter: Repeats the sentence the educator used to teach the word.

nodes.label: Adds two three-digit numbers with regrouping on paper, showing the exchange in the working.
nodes.text: The educator sees the carried ten written in the working, not only the total.
nodes.counter: Writes the correct total with no working shown.

nodes.label: Reads a grade-level passage aloud and answers a question whose answer is stated in the text, reading out the line that says it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the passage read, the answer given, and the line from the text read out as its source.
nodes.counter: Answers from general knowledge and cannot find the line in the text.

nodes.label: Explains a science or geography fact just taught in their own words, with a because.
nodes.text: The educator hears the fact restated differently from the book, with a reason attached.
nodes.counter: Repeats the textbook sentence word for word.

nodes.label: Measures a length or a volume with the right tool and records it with its unit.
nodes.text: The educator sees the tool chosen fit the quantity and the unit written beside the number.
nodes.counter: Writes a number without a unit or with the wrong tool's unit.

nodes.label: Completes a short timed practice set within the time allotted to them and re-works one answer in the margin before handing in.
nodes.text: The educator sees the set finished within the child's allotted time and one answer worked a second time in the margin.
nodes.counter: Finishes early and sits with the sheet untouched until time is called.

nodes.label: Writes a paragraph of four or more sentences on one topic, with a first sentence that says what it is about.
nodes.text: The educator reads a first sentence that announces the topic and sentences that stay on it.
nodes.counter: Writes four sentences on four different things.

nodes.label: Reads a short passage aloud in a taught language that is not their home language and answers one question in it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the reading and the answer both in that language, in its lesson.
nodes.counter: Sounds out the passage correctly, then gives the answer in the language they speak at home.

nodes.label: Asks a question in a lesson that names the exact part they did not understand.
nodes.text: The educator hears the question point to one step, one word or one line, not to the whole topic.
nodes.counter: Asks the educator to explain the whole topic again from the start.

nodes.label: Solves a problem needing three or more steps, laying out each step so another student could follow it.
nodes.text: The educator can follow the working from the first step to the answer without asking.
nodes.counter: Reaches the right answer with steps missing or out of order.

nodes.label: Summarises a textbook chapter in ten sentences that keep its main claims and drop its examples.
nodes.text: The educator reads claims in the child's words and no copied examples.
nodes.counter: Copies the chapter's first sentences in order.

nodes.label: Uses a subject's technical term correctly in an explanation, and gives a plain-words version when asked.
nodes.text: The educator hears the term fit its meaning and a plain version follow on request.
nodes.counter: Uses the term correctly in a rehearsed sentence and cannot give a plain-words version when asked.

nodes.label: Records an experiment's method, readings and result in a table, with units, on the day it is done.
nodes.text: The educator sees the table filled during the practical, units included.
nodes.counter: Writes the expected result before taking the readings.

nodes.label: Sits a full-period written test under exam rules and attempts every question, showing working where asked.
nodes.text: The educator sees every question attempted and working where the paper asks for it.
nodes.counter: Leaves the last questions blank with time remaining.

nodes.label: Writes an essay of several paragraphs that explains a process or event using facts from the unit.
nodes.text: The educator reads paragraphs that each carry a different part of the explanation.
nodes.counter: Writes several paragraphs that restate one point.

nodes.label: Volunteers to work through their own wrong answer on the board with the class, saying where it went wrong.
nodes.text: The educator hears the offer come from the child, then sees them at the board pointing to the step that went wrong.
nodes.counter: Works through the wrong answer at the board because the educator called them up.

nodes.label: Solves an unseen problem in the board's format by choosing which method applies, and writes one line on why that method.
nodes.text: The educator reads a method that fits the problem and a written line giving the reason for choosing it.
nodes.counter: Applies the method just practised whether or not it fits.

nodes.label: Reads a primary source or a research abstract and states its claim and its evidence separately.
nodes.text: The educator sees the claim and the evidence written as two separate things.
nodes.counter: Summarises the source's topic without separating claim from evidence.

nodes.label: Teaches a concept from their own subject to a younger student, using two different explanations.
nodes.text: The educator hears the second explanation differ from the first when the first does not land, and notes it without the younger child's name.
nodes.counter: Reads their notes aloud to the younger student.

nodes.label: Derives a formula or result from first principles on paper, rather than quoting it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the derivation start from definitions, not from the formula.
nodes.counter: Quotes the formula and substitutes numbers.

nodes.label: Completes a full board-pattern examination under exam conditions, managing time across all sections.
nodes.text: The educator sees every section attempted within the time.
nodes.counter: Runs out of time with a whole section unattempted.

nodes.label: Writes an extended piece that argues a position using sources cited by name.
nodes.text: The educator sees named sources and a position that rests on them.
nodes.counter: Lists sources at the end that the argument itself never uses.

nodes.label: Thinking & reasoning
nodes.text: Defines problems, evaluates evidence, reasons quantitatively and changes position when evidence warrants.

nodes.label: Asks a why question about something just seen or heard, such as why the ice melted.
nodes.text: The educator hears a why that follows from the moment, not from a book.
nodes.counter: Asks 'why' again to each answer without waiting to hear it, as a way of keeping the adult talking.

nodes.label: Says what will happen before a simple test, such as which object will sink, and then checks.
nodes.text: The educator hears the prediction before the object touches the water.
nodes.counter: Says the answer after seeing the result.

nodes.label: Gives a reason for a choice when asked, such as why this block goes on the bottom.
nodes.text: The educator hears a reason that refers to the block, not just to wanting it.
nodes.counter: Says 'because' and repeats the choice.

nodes.label: Points out one way two things are the same and one way they differ.
nodes.text: The educator hears both a likeness and a difference named.
nodes.counter: Names only what each thing is.

nodes.label: Changes a guess after seeing a result that does not match it, and says so.
nodes.text: The educator hears the child say the guess was wrong and give the new one.
nodes.counter: Repeats the first guess after seeing the result.

nodes.label: Says which of two events happened first and which one made the other happen, in a story or a game.
nodes.text: The educator hears the order and the cause both stated.
nodes.counter: Lists both events without saying which caused which.

nodes.label: Turns a wondering into a question that can be tested in class, such as does the plant grow faster near the window.
nodes.text: The educator hears a question the class could actually set up and answer.
nodes.counter: Asks a question no one in the room could test.

nodes.label: Writes a prediction before an investigation and the result after, and states whether they matched.
nodes.text: The educator sees the prediction dated before the result.
nodes.counter: Writes the prediction after the result is known.

nodes.label: Backs a claim with one piece of evidence from something read, measured or observed.
nodes.text: The educator hears or reads the evidence named beside the claim.
nodes.counter: Backs a claim with 'everyone knows'.

nodes.label: Spots a pattern in a table or chart, such as one column larger in every row, and says what it might mean.
nodes.text: The educator hears the pattern described and a meaning offered.
nodes.counter: Reads single values from the chart without a pattern.

nodes.label: Changes an answer after new evidence and writes the reason for the change beside it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the old answer, the new one and the reason, all visible.
nodes.counter: Rubs out the first answer so the change is invisible.

nodes.label: Sorts statements about a topic into facts and opinions and explains one sorting.
nodes.text: The educator sees the sort and hears one placement justified.
nodes.counter: Sorts by whether the statement agrees with their own view.

nodes.label: Designs a fair test with one thing changed and the rest kept the same, and names what is kept the same.
nodes.text: The educator sees one variable changed and the controls listed.
nodes.counter: Changes two things at once and reports a result.

nodes.label: Judges whether a source is trustworthy by who wrote it, when and why, before using it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the author, date and purpose noted before the source is cited.
nodes.counter: Uses the first search result without saying who wrote it.

nodes.label: Estimates the size of an answer before calculating and writes whether the calculated result agrees with the estimate.
nodes.text: The educator sees the estimate written above the working and a tick or a note comparing it with the answer.
nodes.counter: Writes an estimate after the calculation that matches the answer exactly.

nodes.label: Names an assumption in an argument, their own or another's, and says what changes if it is false.
nodes.text: The educator hears the assumption named and its consequence traced.
nodes.counter: Restates the argument's conclusion and calls it the assumption.

nodes.label: Concedes a point in a discussion when the other side's evidence is stronger, and says which evidence moved them.
nodes.text: The educator hears the concession and the evidence named.
nodes.counter: Says 'fine, you win' to end the exchange without naming any evidence.

nodes.label: Puts a number on a claim, such as how much faster, and says how it was measured.
nodes.text: The educator sees the number and the measurement it rests on.
nodes.counter: Says 'much faster' without a measurement.

nodes.label: Writes a problem statement that says what is known, what is asked and what would count as solved, before starting.
nodes.text: The educator sees the statement written before any working.
nodes.counter: Starts computing before saying what the question is.

nodes.label: Weighs two sources that disagree and explains in writing which to trust more and why.
nodes.text: The educator reads both sources named and a reasoned choice between them.
nodes.counter: Picks the source that agrees with their first view.

nodes.label: Checks a result by a second method or by trying an extreme case, and reports the check alongside the answer.
nodes.text: The educator sees the second method or the extreme case written beside the answer.
nodes.counter: Reports the answer with a note that it 'seems right'.

nodes.label: Uses a model or a formula to predict a case not yet seen, then compares with a measurement.
nodes.text: The educator sees the prediction made before the measurement and the comparison after.
nodes.counter: Fits a model to data already seen and stops.

nodes.label: Records a change of position on a question in writing, stating the evidence that changed it.
nodes.text: The educator reads the earlier position, the later one and the evidence between.
nodes.counter: Presents the final position as if it had been held from the start.

nodes.label: Identifies the specific flaw in a flawed argument, such as a sample too small or a cause confused with a correlation.
nodes.text: The educator reads the flaw named precisely in the child's written response, such as the sample size or cause confused with correlation.
nodes.counter: Calls the argument 'wrong' without naming the flaw.

nodes.label: Learning & agency
nodes.text: Sets goals, researches independently, seeks feedback, reflects and improves.

nodes.label: Chooses an activity with an end point, such as a puzzle or a painting, at free-choice time and stays with it to the end.
nodes.text: The educator sees the activity chosen unprompted and the puzzle completed or the painting declared done by the child.
nodes.counter: Finishes an activity the educator assigned rather than one they chose themselves.

nodes.label: Tries a task on their own first and then asks for help with the specific part that is hard.
nodes.text: The educator sees an attempt before the request and hears the hard part named.
nodes.counter: Asks for help before touching the task.

nodes.label: Tells an adult one thing they learned or could do today that they could not do before.
nodes.text: The educator hears a learning named, not an activity listed.
nodes.counter: Names an activity done today without what was learned.

nodes.label: Fixes a mistake in their own work after one hint, without the adult doing it for them.
nodes.text: The educator gives one hint and sees the child make the correction.
nodes.counter: Waits for the adult to correct it.

nodes.label: Puts materials back where they belong so the next child can use them, without being told.
nodes.text: The educator sees the materials returned to their place unprompted.
nodes.counter: Puts materials away only when asked by name.

nodes.label: Tries again, in the same session, at something that failed the first time, such as a tower or a jump.
nodes.text: The educator sees the second attempt follow the first failure.
nodes.counter: Tries again after an adult says 'try once more'.

nodes.label: Names something they want to learn to do, such as tying laces or writing a letter, and asks to be shown.
nodes.text: The educator hears the wish named and the request to be shown, unprompted.
nodes.counter: Agrees to learn what the educator proposes.

nodes.label: Writes one learning goal for the week in their own words and marks on Friday whether it was met.
nodes.text: The educator reads a goal in the child's words and sees it reviewed on Friday.
nodes.counter: Copies the class goal from the board.

nodes.label: Looks up an answer in a book, chart or dictionary before asking the educator.
nodes.text: The educator sees the resource opened before the hand goes up.
nodes.counter: Asks the educator the spelling of a word on the word wall.

nodes.label: Names, in a reflection, what was hard about a task and one thing to do differently next time.
nodes.text: The educator reads or hears a specific difficulty and a specific change, and notes that both were named rather than filing the words.
nodes.counter: Writes 'it was easy' or 'it was hard' without a why.

nodes.label: Uses a written comment from the educator to change the next draft, and can point to the change.
nodes.text: The educator sees the commented point changed in the next draft.
nodes.counter: Rewrites the draft without touching the point commented on.

nodes.label: Keeps their own record of practice sheets done and skills mastered, and updates it unprompted.
nodes.text: The educator sees the record current without having asked.
nodes.counter: Fills the record only when the educator checks it.

nodes.label: Chooses the Hard or Advance version of a task when offered a choice of difficulty, and attempts it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the Hard or Advance sheet taken from the choice offered and worked on.
nodes.counter: Chooses the harder version and hands it in blank.

nodes.label: Breaks a multi-week project into dated steps at the start and shows, at a check-in, the steps done so far ticked.
nodes.text: The educator sees the plan dated from the start of the project, with the steps completed so far ticked, at a check-in.
nodes.counter: Writes the plan on the last day.

nodes.label: Finds two sources on a topic without help and notes where each was found.
nodes.text: The educator sees two sources located by the child and their origins noted.
nodes.counter: Notes two sources that were both handed to them by the educator.

nodes.label: Asks a peer or educator for feedback on one named aspect of their work before it is due.
nodes.text: The educator hears the aspect named in the request.
nodes.counter: Asks 'is this good?' about the whole piece.

nodes.label: Marks their own work against the rubric before submitting and notes where it falls short.
nodes.text: The educator sees the self-marking with at least one shortfall named.
nodes.counter: Awards full marks on every line.

nodes.label: Reads their own skill map, names a gap, and chooses practice for it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the gap named and the practice chosen to match it.
nodes.counter: Practises only skills already secure.

nodes.label: Keeps working on a problem after a first attempt fails, trying a different approach within the session.
nodes.text: The educator sees a second, different approach follow the failed one.
nodes.counter: Repeats the same failed approach three times.

nodes.label: Completes an independent study from question to finished product and shows the milestones they set with the date each was met.
nodes.text: The educator sees the finished study and, beside it, the child's own milestones with the dates they were met.
nodes.counter: Presents the product with a plan written in the final week.

nodes.label: Reviews their own bibliography and drops or replaces an unreliable source, saying why.
nodes.text: The educator sees a source removed and the reason recorded.
nodes.counter: Adds sources to lengthen the list.

nodes.label: Seeks feedback from an expert outside school, found by the child or introduced by the school and known to it, and reports what they learned.
nodes.text: The educator knows who was approached and how, and sees the expert's feedback and the change it led to.
nodes.counter: Reports the feedback without any change made.

nodes.label: States a standard for their work above the rubric's, and shows where the work meets it.
nodes.text: The educator reads a standard the rubric did not ask for and sees it met.
nodes.counter: Restates the rubric as their standard.

nodes.label: Learns an unfamiliar tool or topic from documentation or a course on their own, and demonstrates it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the tool used or the topic applied, not described.
nodes.counter: Watches a tutorial and describes it without using the tool.

nodes.label: Returns to a piece of work after a public setback, such as a lost debate or a failed demonstration, and improves it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the work taken up again and changed after the setback.
nodes.counter: Drops the piece after the setback.

nodes.label: Creation & problem solving
nodes.text: Turns ideas into experiments, prototypes, designs, investigations and useful outputs.

nodes.label: Builds something with blocks or junk that matches a plan said aloud beforehand.
nodes.text: The educator hears the plan first and sees the build match it.
nodes.counter: Names what the finished pile is after building it.

nodes.label: Solves a practical problem, such as a bridge that falls, by changing the materials or the design.
nodes.text: The educator sees the change made by the child and the bridge stand.
nodes.counter: Asks an adult to fix the bridge.

nodes.label: Draws a picture that shows an idea or a plan and explains what each part is.
nodes.text: The educator hears each part of the drawing named for what it does.
nodes.counter: Draws and says it is 'just a drawing'.

nodes.label: Invents a new rule for a familiar game and plays a round with it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the rule proposed before play and sees it kept.
nodes.counter: Proposes a new rule and then plays the round by the old rules.

nodes.label: Makes a second version of something made, and says what is different.
nodes.text: The educator sees two versions and hears the difference named.
nodes.counter: Makes the same thing again.

nodes.label: Uses a simple tool, such as scissors, a hole punch or a magnifier, for its purpose without help.
nodes.text: The educator sees the tool used as intended with no hand over hand.
nodes.counter: Holds the tool and asks an adult to use it.

nodes.label: Makes something for a particular person, such as a card or a model, and gives it to them saying who it is for.
nodes.text: The educator sees the thing handed over and hears who it is for.
nodes.counter: Makes a card because the whole class was asked to make one.

nodes.label: Uses one object as another in pretend play, such as a block as a phone, and shows or tells what it stands for.
nodes.text: The educator sees the object used as something else and the child make plain, by word or action, what it is now.
nodes.counter: Uses a toy phone as a phone.

nodes.label: Makes a model or device that does what it was meant to do, such as a lever that lifts a load.
nodes.text: The educator sees the model do its job.
nodes.counter: Presents a model that looks right and does not work.

nodes.label: Tests a design, records what failed and changes one thing before testing again.
nodes.text: The educator sees the failure recorded and one change made.
nodes.counter: Changes everything after a failure.

nodes.label: Writes a materials list and a step plan before making something, and follows it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the list and plan written first and the make follow them.
nodes.counter: Writes the list after making.

nodes.label: Writes an original story of their own with a beginning, a problem and an ending.
nodes.text: The educator reads a plot of the child's own with all three parts.
nodes.counter: Retells a known story with the names changed.

nodes.label: Presents a made thing to the class and says what changed from the first version and why.
nodes.text: The educator hears the change and its reason.
nodes.counter: Shows the thing without saying what was changed.

nodes.label: Chooses the right tool for a job from several available, and says why that one.
nodes.text: The educator hears the reason for the tool chosen.
nodes.counter: Uses whatever tool is nearest.

nodes.label: Builds a prototype that meets a written brief with constraints, such as a budget or a size limit.
nodes.text: The educator checks the prototype against each constraint in the brief.
nodes.counter: Builds something impressive that ignores the constraints.

nodes.label: Keeps an iteration log across several tests with what changed and what the results were.
nodes.text: The educator reads several entries, each with a change and a result.
nodes.counter: Records the final version only.

nodes.label: Fixes a program of their own when a test input breaks it, and shows the failing input and the change made.
nodes.text: The educator sees the input that broke the program and the line changed to fix it.
nodes.counter: Deletes the failing test input so the program passes.

nodes.label: Produces a piece of art, media or performance for a real audience outside the class, such as younger children or parents.
nodes.text: The educator sees the piece reach the audience it was made for.
nodes.counter: Makes the piece for the class display only.

nodes.label: Pitches a solution to a problem and names one trade-off it makes.
nodes.text: The educator hears the trade-off named in the pitch.
nodes.counter: Pitches the solution as having no downside.

nodes.label: Carries out an investigation of an open question with a method they designed, and reports what was found.
nodes.text: The educator sees a method of the child's own and a finding, expected or not.
nodes.counter: Follows a worksheet method and reports the expected answer.

nodes.label: Makes or repairs something that someone in the school asked for, and hands it over working.
nodes.text: The educator sees the person who asked receive it and use it.
nodes.counter: Makes something to a brief the educator set for marks.

nodes.label: Makes an original artwork, composition or performance piece to a set theme and explains one choice made in it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the piece and hears one choice in it explained.
nodes.counter: Copies a piece found online and explains the theme.

nodes.label: Delivers a project to a brief from someone outside school and incorporates their feedback.
nodes.text: The educator sees the outside brief, the delivery and the feedback acted on.
nodes.counter: Delivers to their own brief.

nodes.label: Documents a build or an experiment so another student repeats it without asking questions.
nodes.text: The educator sees another student repeat it from the document alone.
nodes.counter: Documents it so only they can repeat it.

nodes.label: Builds a piece of software with tests, and shows a test catching a bug.
nodes.text: The educator sees a test fail on a bug and pass after the fix.
nodes.counter: Shows working software with no tests.

nodes.label: Finishes a piece of work to exhibition standard and labels it with what it is and what changed from the first version.
nodes.text: The educator sees the finished piece and its label naming the change from the first version.
nodes.counter: Shows the first version with a label saying it is finished.

nodes.label: Completes a real task in a school-arranged and supervised internship or apprenticeship placement, confirmed by the host.
nodes.text: The educator sees the host's confirmation of a task done, at a placement the school vetted and supervises.
nodes.counter: Attends the placement without a completed task.

nodes.label: Designs and runs an original investigation, from question to method to findings, and presents it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the question, method and findings all the child's own.
nodes.counter: Repeats a textbook investigation.

nodes.label: Communication & collaboration
nodes.text: Writes, speaks, presents, listens, negotiates and contributes reliably to teams.

nodes.label: Tells the circle something that happened, in two or more connected sentences in a language they speak, so that listeners can follow.
nodes.text: The educator hears two connected sentences about one piece of news, in whichever language the child uses, with no prompt between them.
nodes.counter: Says one word and stops when asked more.

nodes.label: Listens to a classmate and says something back about what they said.
nodes.text: The educator hears the response refer to the classmate's words.
nodes.counter: Waits for their own turn without responding.

nodes.label: Asks to join a game, and accepts a no or joins in the way agreed.
nodes.text: The educator sees the ask and the answer respected.
nodes.counter: Pushes into the game without asking.

nodes.label: Shows a drawing or a build to the class and explains what it is.
nodes.text: The educator hears the explanation reach the class.
nodes.counter: Holds up the work silently.

nodes.label: Uses words or signs to settle a dispute over a toy or a turn, such as proposing a swap.
nodes.text: The educator hears or sees the proposal made and sees the dispute end.
nodes.counter: Repeats 'give it to me' louder until the other child gives in.

nodes.label: Gives a two-minute prepared talk to the class with a beginning and an end.
nodes.text: The educator hears a shaped talk delivered to the room.
nodes.counter: Reads the talk from the page without looking up.

nodes.label: Adds to a classmate's idea in discussion, naming whose idea it builds on.
nodes.text: The educator hears the classmate credited and the idea extended.
nodes.counter: Repeats the classmate's idea in other words without adding to it.

nodes.label: Agrees roles with a group before a task starts and takes the role agreed.
nodes.text: The educator sees the roles agreed first and kept.
nodes.counter: Takes the role they want and leaves the rest.

nodes.label: Writes a letter or message to a real person for a purpose, such as a request or a thank you.
nodes.text: The educator reads a named recipient and a clear purpose.
nodes.counter: Writes a letter to no one in particular.

nodes.label: Explains their method to a classmate who is stuck, without giving the answer.
nodes.text: The educator hears the method explained and the answer withheld.
nodes.counter: Tells the classmate the answer.

nodes.label: Disagrees with a classmate's answer by giving a reason that addresses the answer, not the classmate, and lets the classmate reply.
nodes.text: The educator hears the disagreement and its reason addressed to the answer, not to the classmate, and the classmate given the floor.
nodes.counter: Says 'you're wrong' without a reason.

nodes.label: Presents to an audience using a visual aid they made, and answers a question from the floor.
nodes.text: The educator sees the aid used and a question answered.
nodes.counter: Reads slides aloud and takes no questions.

nodes.label: Leads a small-group discussion so that every member speaks, and summarises what was agreed.
nodes.text: The educator sees every member speak and hears the summary.
nodes.counter: Speaks most and summarises their own view.

nodes.label: Resolves a disagreement in a group task by proposing an option both sides accept.
nodes.text: The educator sees the option proposed and both sides carry on.
nodes.counter: Gives way to the louder side so that the task can go on.

nodes.label: Writes a piece in a tone suited to a named audience, such as a report for the head or a guide for Grade 3.
nodes.text: The educator reads a tone that fits the audience named.
nodes.counter: Writes in the same tone for every audience.

nodes.label: Gives a classmate written feedback with one strength and one specific change to make.
nodes.text: The educator reads a strength and a change the classmate could act on.
nodes.counter: Writes 'good job' or 'needs work'.

nodes.label: Argues the side assigned to them in a structured debate, using evidence for it, whichever side that is.
nodes.text: The educator hears evidence used for the assigned side and notes that the side was assigned.
nodes.counter: Argues the assigned side with opinions and no evidence.

nodes.label: Presents work to an audience outside school, such as parents, a partner organisation or a competition panel, and handles questions.
nodes.text: The educator sees the outside audience and questions handled.
nodes.counter: Presents only to classmates.

nodes.label: Runs a meeting with an agenda and leaves it with actions assigned to named people.
nodes.text: The educator reads the agenda and the actions with names.
nodes.counter: Holds a meeting with no record of what was decided.

nodes.label: Negotiates an outcome with adults, such as a change to a school routine, presenting a case and reaching an agreed outcome with them.
nodes.text: The educator sees the case made, the adults' response answered, and an outcome both sides state as agreed.
nodes.counter: Complains about the routine without proposing a case.

nodes.label: Writes a formal document, such as a proposal, a report or an application, that a stranger could act on.
nodes.text: The educator gives the document to someone uninvolved and sees them act on it.
nodes.counter: Writes a document that needs the author present to explain it.

nodes.label: Runs a mentoring session with a younger student, in a pairing the school set up, and adds it to a log of earlier dated sessions.
nodes.text: The educator sees the session take place and the log with earlier dated entries, kept without the younger child's name or difficulties.
nodes.counter: Logs a first meeting as mentoring.

nodes.label: Restates an opposing view to its holder's satisfaction before answering it, in a discussion.
nodes.text: The educator hears the holder agree the restatement is fair.
nodes.counter: Answers an opposing view without restating it.

nodes.label: Technology & AI
nodes.text: Uses digital tools productively; verifies AI outputs; understands bias, privacy, provenance and limitations.

nodes.label: Operates a simple screen-free device, such as a story player or a torch, for a stated purpose, with an adult present.
nodes.text: The educator sees the device used for the purpose the child stated and put down afterwards.
nodes.counter: Taps a device at random.

nodes.label: Follows a three-step sequence of instructions, given in a language they understand, in order, such as in a coding game played without a screen.
nodes.text: The educator gives the steps in a language the child understands and sees the three done in the order given.
nodes.counter: Does the steps in a different order.

nodes.label: Gives a classmate step-by-step instructions to move across a grid, and corrects one wrong step.
nodes.text: The educator hears the steps and sees one corrected.
nodes.counter: Says 'go there' and points.

nodes.label: Says whether a picture or a story is real or made up, and gives one reason.
nodes.text: The educator hears the judgement and a reason for it.
nodes.counter: Says real or pretend without a reason.

nodes.label: Asks before using a classmate's crayons, drawing or belongings.
nodes.text: The educator hears the ask before the crayons or the drawing are touched.
nodes.counter: Asks only after already picking the thing up.

nodes.label: Uses a digital tool to produce a piece of work, such as a typed paragraph or a chart from data they collected.
nodes.text: The educator sees the finished piece made with the tool.
nodes.counter: Uses the tool to play during work time.

nodes.label: Writes a short block-based program and fixes it when it does not do what was intended.
nodes.text: The educator sees the program misbehave and the child change it until it works.
nodes.counter: Runs a sample program without changing it.

nodes.label: Explains in plain words what a short set of instructions or program will do before running it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the prediction before the run.
nodes.counter: Runs it and then describes what happened.

nodes.label: Checks an answer from a search or an AI tool against a book or a second source before using it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the second source opened before the answer is used.
nodes.counter: Copies the first answer given.

nodes.label: Says what should not be shared online, such as full name, address or school, and applies it in a task.
nodes.text: The educator sees the private fields left out in the task.
nodes.counter: Types their full name and address into a form without asking.

nodes.label: Names where an image or fact came from when using it in their work.
nodes.text: The educator sees the source named beside the image or fact.
nodes.counter: Uses an image with no source.

nodes.label: Writes or dictates step-by-step instructions for a classmate to draw a figure, then changes a step when the drawing does not match what was meant.
nodes.text: The educator sees the steps, the drawing they produced and the step rewritten after it; the filed artefact is the child's own instruction sheet, not the classmate's drawing.
nodes.counter: Draws the figure for the classmate instead of rewriting the step.

nodes.label: Chooses a digital tool suited to a task, such as a spreadsheet for data, and justifies the choice.
nodes.text: The educator hears the justification and sees the tool fit.
nodes.counter: Uses the same tool for everything.

nodes.label: Writes a text-based program with a loop and a condition that solves a set problem.
nodes.text: The educator sees the loop and condition in the code and the problem solved.
nodes.counter: Writes straight-line code with no loop.

nodes.label: Checks an AI tool's output claim by claim against a source, marking each claim confirmed or corrected and naming the source used.
nodes.text: The educator sees each claim marked confirmed or corrected and the source used written beside the marks.
nodes.counter: Marks every claim confirmed without opening a source.

nodes.label: Explains, with an example, how an app's recommendation or an AI answer can be biased by its data.
nodes.text: The educator hears a concrete example, not a slogan.
nodes.counter: Says 'AI is biased' without an example.

nodes.label: Sets privacy settings on a school account as taught and explains what each setting protects.
nodes.text: The educator sees the settings set and hears each one explained.
nodes.counter: Leaves defaults and cannot say what they do.

nodes.label: States where AI was used in their work and where it was not, when handing it in.
nodes.text: The educator reads the attribution on the submitted work.
nodes.counter: Writes 'used AI' on the cover sheet with no indication of where.

nodes.label: Builds a working digital product, such as a website, app or automation, for a real user, and gets their feedback.
nodes.text: The educator sees the user use it and the feedback recorded.
nodes.counter: Builds a demo no one uses.

nodes.label: Writes a program that reads real data, uses a ready-made code library, and produces a checked result.
nodes.text: The educator sees the check that the result is right.
nodes.counter: Produces output with no check that it is right.

nodes.label: Uses AI in a piece of work with a log of prompts, what was kept, what was rejected and why.
nodes.text: The educator reads the log beside the work.
nodes.counter: Keeps the prompts but not what was rejected or why.

nodes.label: Evaluates a technology's benefits and harms for a named group, with evidence, and takes a position.
nodes.text: The educator reads the weighing and the position taken.
nodes.counter: Lists benefits and harms without weighing them.

nodes.label: Completes a task without AI that they could have done with it, and writes two lines on what doing it alone showed.
nodes.text: The educator sees the task done unaided and reads the two lines beneath it.
nodes.counter: Does the task unaided because AI was not allowed, and says nothing about what it showed.

nodes.label: Handles other people's data in a project according to a stated rule, such as consent and deletion, and shows the rule was followed.
nodes.text: The educator sees the rule stated and evidence it was kept.
nodes.counter: States a consent rule at the start and keeps the data after the project ends.

nodes.label: Self & relationships
nodes.text: Shows resilience, emotional regulation, physical competence, empathy and responsible independence.

nodes.label: Names what they feel after a fall, a dispute or a lost game, in their own words, and chooses what to do next.
nodes.text: The educator hears a feeling named in the child's own words and sees the choice made; the note records the choice, never the words or the cause.
nodes.counter: Is told by an adult what they are feeling and repeats it.

nodes.label: Waits for a turn on the slide or with a toy without a reminder from an adult.
nodes.text: The educator sees the wait with no adult prompt.
nodes.counter: Waits only after an adult says their name.

nodes.label: Notices a classmate who is hurt or crying and does something for them, such as fetching an adult or sitting with them.
nodes.text: The educator sees the noticing and the act that follows.
nodes.counter: Joins the crowd around the hurt classmate to look, without doing anything for them.

nodes.label: Manages their own bag, bottle and shoes at arrival and departure without an adult doing it for them, using any aids they have.
nodes.text: The educator sees the bag, bottle and shoes handled by the child, with their own aids if any, and no adult's hands on them.
nodes.counter: Holds out a foot for an adult to put the shoe on.

nodes.label: Returns to play after a small hurt or a lost game, once looked after.
nodes.text: The educator sees the child back in play in the same session.
nodes.counter: Returns to play only when an adult walks them back to the game.

nodes.label: Takes a full turn in an outdoor running or climbing game, moving in the way their own body moves.
nodes.text: The educator sees the child take the turn from start to finish, with any aid they use.
nodes.counter: Runs onto the field with the others and stands watching them take the turn.

nodes.label: Tells a classmate 'stop' or 'I am still using it', in words or signs, when the classmate reaches for or takes what they are using.
nodes.text: The educator hears or sees the words or sign given to the classmate before any adult steps in; the note holds the child's words, never the incident or the classmate.
nodes.counter: Says 'stop' only after the educator has told the classmate to stop.

nodes.label: Uses a strategy learned in class, such as breathing or stepping away, before responding in a conflict.
nodes.text: The educator sees the strategy used in the moment, before the response, and notes the strategy alone, not the conflict or who else was in it.
nodes.counter: Names the strategy afterwards but did not use it.

nodes.label: Keeps an agreement made with a classmate, such as a swap or a promise, without an adult enforcing it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the agreement honoured with no adult involved.
nodes.counter: Keeps the agreement only when reminded.

nodes.label: Invites a child standing alone at the edge of a game or group to join, before any adult suggests it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the child alone at the edge and the invitation come from the classmate first.
nodes.counter: Invites the child when an adult asks the group to.

nodes.label: Does their class responsibility, such as watering the plants, on a day when nobody reminded them, using their own way of remembering.
nodes.text: The educator sees the job done before anyone has mentioned it that day, whatever memory aid the child uses.
nodes.counter: Does the job after the educator glances at the job chart.

nodes.label: Shows a physical skill, such as skipping or catching, that an earlier record shows they could not yet do.
nodes.text: The educator sees the skill done unaided and finds the earlier note saying the child could not yet do it.
nodes.counter: Shows a skill they arrived at school already able to do.

nodes.label: Accepts losing a game or a contest and congratulates the winner.
nodes.text: The educator hears the congratulation given to the winner.
nodes.counter: Shakes the winner's hand only when an adult tells the players to.

nodes.label: Goes back to a classmate after a conflict to apologise or to sort it out, without being sent.
nodes.text: The educator sees the approach made unprompted and notes the repair alone, not the conflict or the classmate.
nodes.counter: Apologises when the educator stands beside them and waits for it.

nodes.label: Delivers their agreed part to a team, such as attending a practice or handing in a section, on the date the team set.
nodes.text: The educator sees the team's plan with the date and the part delivered on it.
nodes.counter: Attends the sessions but leaves their part for others to deliver.

nodes.label: Speaks up when a classmate is being excluded or mocked, in the moment.
nodes.text: The educator hears the intervention as it happens and notes the speaking up alone; the mocking itself goes to the school's own process, not this record.
nodes.counter: Joins the classmate's side once an adult has already stepped in.

nodes.label: Hands in a piece of work on its due date with the deadline written in their own planner the week before.
nodes.text: The educator sees the planner entry dated at least a week earlier and the work in on the day.
nodes.counter: Hands work in on time with a planner filled in that morning.

nodes.label: Shows a training record for a goal about what they can do, such as a distance, with attempts dated across four or more weeks.
nodes.text: The educator reads the goal and attempt entries spanning four or more weeks, a record of what was done, never a body measure.
nodes.counter: Records one attempt on the last day.

nodes.label: Tells the educator before a deadline that a piece of work will be late and proposes a new date.
nodes.text: The educator hears it before the date, with a new date offered.
nodes.counter: Explains why the work is late after the deadline has passed.

nodes.label: Takes on part of a classmate's share of a team task after the classmate says they cannot finish it, and tells the team.
nodes.text: The educator hears the classmate say so, sees the extra part done and hears the team told; the note names the part taken on, not the classmate or why.
nodes.counter: Does the whole task alone without telling the team.

nodes.label: Mediates between two classmates in conflict so that both agree a way forward.
nodes.text: The educator sees both classmates accept the way forward and notes the mediation alone, not the dispute or who was in it.
nodes.counter: Takes one side.

nodes.label: Leads a team through a setback, such as a failed event, by re-planning with the team.
nodes.text: The educator sees the re-plan made with the team present.
nodes.counter: Assigns blame and re-plans alone.

nodes.label: Raises an unfairness affecting others through a school channel, such as council, and follows it through.
nodes.text: The educator sees the matter raised in the channel and followed up, and notes the raising, not the complaint's content; a concern about an adult goes to the safeguarding lead instead.
nodes.counter: Complains privately and lets it drop.

nodes.label: Shows a term plan that holds both exam preparation and a project, with a dated change made after something slipped.
nodes.text: The educator reads the plan, the dated change and what prompted it.
nodes.counter: Shows a plan written after the term ended.

nodes.label: Brings their own dated record of a physical practice kept across the year and names one change in it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the child's own dated record and hears one change named from it.
nodes.counter: Speaks about the practice in general terms with no record to show.

nodes.label: Brings a classmate who missed a session up to date on what was agreed and what they missed, without being asked.
nodes.text: The educator sees the catch-up happen before the next session, unprompted.
nodes.counter: Forwards the notes when the classmate asks for them.

nodes.label: Stops an argument that has reached raised voices by proposing a break and a time to return to it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the break proposed with a time to return and sees the argument pause; the note holds the proposal, not the argument or who was in it.
nodes.counter: Walks away from the argument without a word about returning.

nodes.label: Society, ethics & planet
nodes.text: Can examine trade-offs, understand systems and consider consequences beyond the self.

nodes.label: Waters a plant or feeds the class animal on their day, and checks it is alright.
nodes.text: The educator sees the care given and the check made.
nodes.counter: Waters it when an adult hands over the can.

nodes.label: Puts waste into the right bin, wet, dry or paper, without prompting.
nodes.text: The educator watches the bins after snack and sees the right one chosen with nobody pointing.
nodes.counter: Puts waste in the nearest bin.

nodes.label: Shares a material, such as crayons or blocks, with a classmate who has none, without being asked.
nodes.text: The educator sees the share come from the child.
nodes.counter: Shares after an adult says 'share'.

nodes.label: Says what would be fair for everyone when a share or a turn is in dispute, including a child who is not their friend.
nodes.text: The educator hears a fairness that applies to everyone, including a child the speaker was not playing with.
nodes.counter: Says fair means getting their own way.

nodes.label: Turns off a tap left running or a light left on in an empty room, with nobody asking.
nodes.text: The educator sees the tap or switch closed by the child before anyone speaks.
nodes.counter: Turns it off when the educator points at it.

nodes.label: Picks up litter that is not their own from the playground and puts it in the bin.
nodes.text: The educator sees litter picked up that the child did not drop.
nodes.counter: Puts their own wrapper in the bin.

nodes.label: Votes in a class choice and goes along with the result when their choice loses.
nodes.text: The educator sees the vote cast and the child join the chosen activity after their choice lost.
nodes.counter: Joins the winning activity having voted for it.

nodes.label: Handles a living thing found outdoors, such as a snail or a worm, gently and puts it back where it was.
nodes.text: The educator sees the creature handled without harm and returned to its place.
nodes.counter: Keeps the creature in a box to show the class later.

nodes.label: Reports a figure they measured about the school's use of water, paper or power, and says how they measured it.
nodes.text: The educator hears the figure, what it is about, and how it was measured.
nodes.counter: Reports a figure found online about schools in general.

nodes.label: Proposes and carries out one way to reduce waste in a class activity and checks whether it worked.
nodes.text: The educator sees the change made and the check afterwards.
nodes.counter: Proposes a way and does not try it.

nodes.label: Explains a school or class rule by the reason for it, not just 'because it is the rule'.
nodes.text: The educator hears the reason, not the rule repeated.
nodes.counter: Says the rule is the rule.

nodes.label: Names who else is affected by a decision in a story or a class choice, beyond themselves.
nodes.text: The educator hears others named and how they are affected.
nodes.counter: Names only how it affects them.

nodes.label: Does a task that helps someone outside the class, such as reading to younger children, and reports it.
nodes.text: The educator sees the task done and the report.
nodes.counter: Helps a classmate inside the class and reports it as service.

nodes.label: Collects data on a local issue, such as traffic or water at school, and presents the findings to those who can act on them.
nodes.text: The educator sees the findings presented to a person or body who can act on the issue, not only to the class.
nodes.counter: Presents the findings to the class only, with no one who could act on them in the room.

nodes.label: Sets out both sides of a real decision, such as cost against waste, before recommending one, and names who bears the cost.
nodes.text: The educator reads both sides set out and the person or group who bears the cost named.
nodes.counter: Recommends the option with no downside named.

nodes.label: States the strongest case for each side of a civic question before giving their own view.
nodes.text: The educator hears each side made well before the child's view, and notes the two cases made, not the view the child gave.
nodes.counter: Gives their own view and a token version of the other side.

nodes.label: Changes a plan after seeing that it would harm someone else, and says why.
nodes.text: The educator sees the change and hears the reason.
nodes.counter: Keeps the plan and apologises later.

nodes.label: Organises a service activity with classmates, from plan to delivery, for people outside school.
nodes.text: The educator sees the plan and the delivery, with the people served described and not photographed or named.
nodes.counter: Joins a service activity organised by adults.

nodes.label: Owns a mistake that affected others, tells those affected and puts it right.
nodes.text: The educator sees those affected told and the repair made, and notes the owning and the repair, not the mistake's detail or who was affected.
nodes.counter: Puts it right quietly without telling those affected.

nodes.label: Models a system, such as the school's water or a market, with its feedback loops, and uses it to explain an outcome.
nodes.text: The educator sees feedback loops in the model and an outcome explained by them.
nodes.counter: Draws a diagram with arrows and no feedback.

nodes.label: Applies an ethical framework to a real dilemma, names the trade-offs, decides and defends it.
nodes.text: The educator reads the framework applied, the trade-offs and the defence.
nodes.counter: Decides on instinct and adds a framework label.

nodes.label: Engages a public body, business or community group on an issue through the school, with a documented exchange.
nodes.text: The educator sees the exchange documented, sent through the school and carrying no home address or personal details of the child.
nodes.counter: Writes a letter that is never sent.

nodes.label: Changes something they do at school, such as printing or single-use packaging, after seeing evidence of its harm, and names the evidence.
nodes.text: The educator sees the changed practice at school and hears the evidence named.
nodes.counter: Pledges the change publicly and shows a log begun the day before.

nodes.label: Presents the term's record of a service commitment they led, showing what changed for the people served.
nodes.text: The educator reads dated entries across the term and a stated change for those served, written without their names or private circumstances.
nodes.counter: Runs a one-day event and reports it as sustained.

nodes.label: Holds a public role in the school, such as council or event lead, and accounts for decisions to those affected.
nodes.text: The educator sees the accounting made to those affected.
nodes.counter: Holds the role and reports to adults only.
